illustration_prompt: An extreme close-up of a single tall glass office building at night, cropped tightly by the frame. The building facade fills the scene, with a repeating grid of dark windows showing a few lit ones. In the reflection on the glass, a barely visible thin new moon and a few stars appear, along with the faint ghost of a passing pedestrian below. The sky is clear and dark, with a soft cool night air suggested by the crisp reflections. The composition is cropped close, focusing on the quiet after-dark detail of office lights and the reflected night sky. No text, letters, numbers, signs, or logos.

  strategy below; it may intentionally emphasize only two or three inks.
- NEVER use any other colour: no blue, green, teal, purple, pink, brown, orange,
  or grey. Render everything in the four inks -- a sky becomes flat white, black,
  or yellow (never blue); water becomes black or white; foliage becomes black or
  yellow. Foreign colours turn to muddy speckle on the panel.
- No gradients, soft shading, or grey mid-tones -- the panel can only dither them
  into noise. Build tone and texture using deliberate ink marks such as hatching,
  dots, rough edges, carved gaps, or repeated shapes when the selected style
  calls for them. Keep those marks large enough to survive the display.
- Preserve a strong readable silhouette or value structure from across a room,
  while allowing the selected style to control detail, texture, and line quality.
- Absolutely NO TEXT, letters, numbers, logos, or watermarks.
- The weather mood must read at a glance from across a room.
